correctness.rationale: The only new analytic estimate bounds the first Poisson harmonic subject to vanishing third harmonic. Poisson characteristic functions give asymptotic equidistribution uniformly under a varying angular shift for irrational phi/pi. The pointwise first-plus-third harmonic majorant integrates exactly using one sign change at 7pi/18 and gives J=2(2cos(pi/9)-1)/pi. The binomial transform normalizations and Bouthat Lemmas 4.2, 5.1, and 3.2 transfer J to 2J. Zero-factor and complex-to-real cases are included. Independent checker tests finite identities and integral but is not substituted for the proof.
risks: The proof uses the named Phragmen–Lindelof and two-saddle lemmas in the inspected primary paper; their hypotheses were compared with the normalized functions. No explicit convergence rate in irrational angle is claimed.

value.rationale: The globally sharp bound is attained at a rational phase, but this exact theorem strictly strengthens it on the full-measure irrational-phase class. The harmonic certificate provides a general mechanism separating arithmetic resonance from generic Poisson angular averaging. It establishes a structural parameter-dependent improvement in a live sharp-constant problem rather than a standalone finite computation; no fixed-parameter optimality is claimed.
risks: The numerical improvement is modest, approximately three percent; mathematical value relies on full-measure parameter structure and exact transfer, not the percentage alone.
